walkthrough: Goal: open the app and know what to practise today: stage 1 of V大's course, single lines and single colours, a session of 20 to 30 minutes, my colours against my earlier sessions, then one more if I like.

Entry: the gallery's first card is 'Today', a sheet with 'Stage 1 · Lines and colours', how many sessions I finished of about 15, and 'Start practice' (or 'Continue practice' while a session is open). Tap it: a practice sheet grows out of the card. It is not an artwork: it never shows among the cards, keeps no versions and lives as long as the session's record.

The sheet: the app lays out the exercises itself, one pair of frames at a time, revealed as I go: the original in the left frame, the empty frame beside it the same size. The view sits on the pair, large but not filling the screen; I zoom, pan and turn as on any canvas. The pill in the middle of the top band reads 'Line 1 of 6' with How, Compare and Next. The first time each kind comes up, a card at the right says how to practise it (How brings it back; Got it closes it).

This walk-through practises with the full interface: All tools, after Gallery at the top left, brings back every island and the side bar on the sheet (S76's walk-through has the exercise's own tools).

Line copy (6 a session, near-straight first, then arcs, S-curves and hooks; then 4 groups of combined lines, S79): I look at the original, find its ends and its most bent points against the frame, and draw it in the empty frame with the pen, my brush, at full speed. StreamLine and QuickShape stay off: the stroke keeps exactly what the pen did. Strokes stay inside the empty frame; a pen landing anywhere else draws nothing and the notice says 'Draw in the empty frame.' Undo, redo, the eraser and the layers work as always; to correct, I draw over the wrong line rather than erase.

Compare: tap Compare: the original lies over my copy in a thick semi-transparent red, and the card at the right holds In place and Aligned (no numbers for lines, and no words on what the red means: How says that once). A stroke drawn after Compare is a correction: the red goes as the pen lands, and Compare shows it again.
Next: the view glides to the next pair, keeping my zoom and turn; the card and overlay go. Next is there before Compare too: an exercise left uncompared is skipped and stores no result.

Colour match (6 a session, most of them low in saturation): a swatch in the left frame. I name it to myself (hue, how pure, how light), pick once by eye on the colour panel and fill the empty frame by dragging the colour into it (or paint it with an opaque brush); the fill stays inside the frame. I compare by eye (redder or yellower, lighter or darker, purer or greyer) and correct two or three times. The eyedropper cannot read the swatch before Compare ('The original can be picked after Compare.'). Compare: each colour shows as a patch inside the other, and the card shows both on the colour wheel and, under it, the colour table: ΔE, then lightness, chroma and hue, each a bar from the original's red line to mine and its number, no sentence. After Compare the eyedropper reads the swatch.

Summary: Next on the last exercise reads Finish; tapped, the view settles on the whole sheet, the pill reads 'Session 1 done' with One more, and the card shows what I compared and my colour judgement beside my earlier sessions in this stage.

One more: a fresh sheet with new exercises opens at its first pair, with the exercise's own tools. Gallery takes me back to the cards, the sheet going into the Today card, which now counts one session done and offers to continue the open one.

After a restart the open practice sheet comes back at the exercise I was on, its compared results and my strokes kept; the Today card keeps its count. Every result is stored with its exercise's kind, seed, the time and, for a colour, its numbers.

Not here (S79 has them): the warm-up of the second session on; other stages, re-tests, drills, trajectories, picture packs; exporting a sheet shows my strokes and fills only (the originals are drawn by the app over the canvas).
